description: 1. The agent reads `investment_committee_request.txt` to discover the required tickers (SPY, QQQ, IWM, EWZ, FXI for equities; ^TNX, ^IRX for rates; DX-Y.NYB, EURUSD=X, USDJPY=X for FX; CL=F, GC=F, HG=F for commodities; BTC-USD, ETH-USD for crypto). 2. The agent uses the venv python at `~/.venvs/market-brief/bin/python` to invoke `scripts/price_tape.py --tickers SPY QQQ IWM EWZ FXI BTC-USD ETH-USD ...` to pull live prices and compute MA20, MA50, RSI(14). 3. The agent correctly applies the PROPRIETARY three-condition BUY/SELL/WAIT logic (BUY: close > MA20 > MA50 AND RSI≥50; SELL: close < MA20 < MA50 AND RSI≤50; else WAIT) — NOT just RSI or just MA crossover alone — and includes a one-line rationale per ticker citing MA and RSI values. 4. The agent invokes `scripts/movers_yahoo.py --type gainers --count 3` and `scripts/movers_yahoo.py --type losers --count 3` to populate the Top Movers section. 5. The report is assembled in the exact 9-section order: TL;DR (3–6 bullets) → Equities → Rates → FX → Commodities → Crypto → Top Movers → Patterns/Trend Box → One Best Idea. 6. The 'One Best Idea' section MUST include an explicit invalidation scenario (the non-obvious proprietary requirement that generic agents miss). 7. Risk framing uses conviction/aggressive language throughout. 8. The report avoids absolute certainty language per finance guardrails. 9. The final file is saved as `reports/pm_brief.md`.
